items.title: Breaking: Optus sued in Federal Court over network outage
items.description: The Australian Communications and Media Authority is suing Optus in the Federal Court over last year's network outage in which hundreds of calls failed to reach Triple Zero.

items.title: Federal Labor MP Luke Gosling arrested over alleged assault
items.description: Federal Labor MP Luke Gosling has been arrested by NT Police over an alleged assault on NT Administrator David Connolly at a Thai festival earlier this month. Mr Gosling remains in custody.

items.title: Live: eSafety Commissioner takes Telegram to court over alleged terrorist content
items.description: The eSafety Commissioner is taking online messaging platform Telegram to court over allegedly hosting terrorist content. Follow live.

items.title: Tasmanian producer pulls products after Four Corners report
items.description: The labels on some of Tasmanian producer Stuart Young's handcrafted goods say some ingredients may come from "further afield". But that was a reference to the Australian mainland, not China.

items.title: Family of three dies in 'ferocious' Sydney granny flat fire
items.description: A family was living within a granny flat where three bodies were found during a fire in Sydney's south-west overnight, New South Wales Police say.

items.title: Why Jim Chalmers is cautious but upbeat
items.description: After delivering a pre-election prediction that "the worst of the inflation challenge is behind us", only to see inflation then steadily rise, Treasurer Jim Chalmers is now more cautious.

items.title: Police investigation finds 'no human remains' in SA's far north
items.description: Police earlier said a member of the public located "what they thought could be human remains in a mine shaft" at Andamooka.

items.title: Liberals registered dead and ex-members as preselectors for key seat
items.description: A leaked Liberal Party spreadsheet has revealed that one dead person and two ex-members were registered as preselectors for a vote in a key seat for the upcoming Victorian election.

items.title: With a Caspian Sea strike, Zelenskyy showed Trump he was a 'winner'
items.description: A large inland sea connecting military supply lines through Russia and Iran could now be a pivotal theatre for two major wars that are usually thought of as separate.

items.title: Deadly H5N1 bird flu strain detected in Victoria for first time
items.description: The deadly H5N1 bird flu strain has reached Victoria after a positive test in a bird was detected in the state's south-west. Agriculture Victoria has confirmed the virus was detected in a greater crested tern found near Portland.

items.title: Woman faces legal action over video of driver in racist road rage incident
items.description: A woman who filmed a Provac Australia driver making an apparent racist gesture to her rideshare driver faces legal action from a company directed by a former One Nation candidate.

items.title: Airborne car becomes wedged in side of Brisbane bus
items.description: Police have launched an investigation after a car became wedged in the side of a bus in Brisbane's south. Emergency services were called to the intersection of Beaudesert and Granard Roads in Rocklea at about 6:30pm yesterday, following reports a hatchback had become airborne and struck a Brisbane City Council bus. The driver of the car was taken to hospital in shock. The bus driver was not hurt. A Brisbane City Council spokeswoman confirmed there were no passengers on the bus at the time.

items.title: Queenslander could face execution over alleged killing of Australian in Syria
items.description: A 20-year-old Gold Coast mobile phone technician is facing a possible death penalty in Syria for the alleged shooting murder of another Australian.

items.title: 'Breaks your heart': Families confront youth detention realities
items.description: New data shows First Nations children are spending longer behind bars without a sentence. Families and experts say the system is failing young people.

items.title: After two years shuttered, Brett Whiteley Studio reopens, just as he left it
items.description: An Archibald winner, an intimate portrait of a marriage and a suburban backyard are among the Brett Whiteley artworks on display at his renovated studio.

items.title: Navigating shifting political views in romantic relationships
items.description: But experts say if morals are involved, it might be a relationship "deal breaker".

items.title: Two-decade-old Toyota Corolla stuns Gibb River Road onlookers
items.description: Jonny Charles is venturing across the famous Kimberley four-wheel-drive track in a 2002 Toyota Corolla, selling coffees out of his boot to fund the trip.

items.title: Pharmaceutical company bows to pressure, offers life-saving drug for free
items.description: Breast cancer patients were considering removing their ovaries until the maker of Zoladex 3.6mg said they would give the drug away rather than list it on the PBS.

items.title: Rise of Ben Carroll 'destroyed' Victorian Labor's Socialist Left, insiders say
items.description: Ben Carroll emerged from a meeting of the Labor caucus on Tuesday as the party's new leader, but what the public did not see was a two-hour fight behind closed doors to decide who would run the state.

items.title: Live: Wall Street sinks after a divided Fed keeps rates on hold, ASX slips
items.description: It was a wild night on Wall Street with all key indices closing sharply lower after the Fed kept rates on hold. The ASX has opened lower. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Quick hits: Swimmer spurns Love Island offer, dictator's grandson's vow
items.description: A Scottish swimmer rejects an approach to appear on a dating reality show and Idi Amin's grandson reveals his royal plans. Here are the quick hits from day six of the Commonwealth Games.

items.title: Broncos premiership prop announces medical retirement due to blood clots
items.description: Brisbane Broncos premiership prop Corey Jensen says goodbye to the NRL after being forced to retire on medical advice.

items.title: Number of children in residential care in Qld jumps to record new highs
items.description: The Queensland government has handed down its response to the Child Safety Inquiry, as shocking new data shows a major increase in children in residential care.

items.title: Neil the seal's damage bill and management costs revealed
items.description: The cost of managing Neil the seal's biannual visits to Tasmania is in the tens of thousands of dollars, the environment department has revealed.

items.title: Library book returned after 150 years, $28k fine waived
items.description: A NSW library has a book returned rather late, but the policy of fining people for the offence was dropped at some point during the 150 years since it was borrowed.
